column1: 24:1|Look! The **LORD** is emptying the earth, laying it waste,\ntwisting its surface and scattering its people.|Keep earth-wide devastation and four actions.

24:2|It will be the same for people and priest,
slave and master, slave woman and mistress,
buyer and seller, lender and borrower,
creditor and debtor.|Preserve six paired social relationships and specific female slavery.
24:3|The earth will be utterly emptied,\nutterly plundered,\nfor the **LORD** has spoken this word.|Repeat emphatic destruction and speech authority.
24:4|The earth mourns and withers;\nthe world droops and withers;\nthe earth’s highest people droop.|Keep repeated withering and height image.

24:5|The earth is defiled beneath its inhabitants,\nfor they have crossed the boundaries of instruction,\nviolated the statute, broken the everlasting covenant.|Retain three transgressions and covenant without naming a specific covenant.

24:6|So a curse devours the earth,
and its inhabitants bear their guilt.
So earth’s inhabitants are scorched,
and few people remain.|Keep doubled consequence, guilt, and scorching.
24:7|New wine mourns, the vine droops;\nall the lighthearted sigh.|Retain personified wine and reversal of joy.
24:8|The tambourines’ joy has stopped,\nthe revelers’ noise has ceased,\nthe lyre’s joy has stopped.|Repeat stopped joy and retain instruments.
24:9|They no longer drink wine with a song;\nstrong drink tastes bitter to those who drink it.|Keep changed drinking experience.
24:10|The city of emptiness is shattered;\nevery house is shut against entry.|Retain tohu emptiness and shut houses.
24:11|In the streets people cry out for wine.\nAll gladness has darkened;\nearth’s joy has gone into exile.|Keep darkness and exile as joy images.
24:12|Only desolation remains in the city;\nits gate is battered into ruins.|Retain gate as concrete civic destruction.
24:13|So it will be within the earth, among the peoples:\nas when an olive tree is beaten,\nas with gleanings when the grape harvest ends.|Keep remnant through two harvest comparisons.
24:14|They lift their voices and sing for joy;\nfrom the west they shout at the **LORD**’s majesty.|Preserve unexplained they and sea/west direction.
24:15|So honor the **LORD** in the east,\nthe name of the **LORD**, Israel’s God,\nin the islands of the sea.|Keep both divine names and geographic reach.

24:16|From earth’s edge we hear songs: “Splendor to the righteous!”
But I say, “I waste away! I waste away! Woe to me!
The treacherous betray;
the treacherous betray with treachery!”|Preserve sudden lament and intensive betrayal repetition.
24:17|Terror, pit, and trap await you,\ninhabitant of the earth.|Retain threefold threat and singular address.

24:18|Whoever flees the sound of terror will fall into the pit;
whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the trap.
The windows on high have opened,
and earth’s foundations shake.|Keep chained escape failures and flood-like windows.
24:19|The earth breaks apart,\nthe earth splits open,\nthe earth shakes violently.|Keep three intensified clauses.

24:20|The earth reels like a drunkard,
sways like a shelter.
Its rebellion weighs heavily upon it;
it falls and will not rise again.|Retain drunkard, shelter, and moral weight.
24:21|On that day the **LORD** will call to account\nthe host on high, on high,\nand earth’s kings, on earth.|Preserve matched heavenly and earthly realms.
24:22|They will be gathered like prisoners into a pit,\nshut away in a prison,\nand after many days they will be visited.|Leave visitation open rather than specify release or punishment.

24:23|The moon will be abashed and the sun ashamed,
for the **LORD** of hosts will reign
on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
and glory will be before his elders.|Preserve celestial shame and elders without identifying them.

25:1|**LORD**, you are my God.
I will exalt you and praise your name,
for you have done wonders—
plans from long ago, faithfully fulfilled.|Keep personal praise and ancient faithful plans.

25:2|You have made a city a heap,
a fortified town a ruin.
The foreigners’ palace is a city no more;
it will never be rebuilt.|Retain unnamed city and irreversible ruin.
25:3|So a strong people will honor you;\nthe city of ruthless nations will fear you.|Keep strength and ruthlessness distinct.

25:4|You have been a refuge for the poor,
a refuge for the needy in distress,
a shelter from the storm, a shade from the heat.
For the breath of the ruthless is like a storm against a wall,|Keep poor/needy repetition and storm-wall text.

25:5|like heat in a dry place.
You subdue the foreigners’ uproar;
as heat is subdued by a cloud’s shade,
the song of the ruthless is brought low.|Retain heat-shade comparison across verse boundary.

25:6|On this mountain the **LORD** of hosts will prepare
a feast for all peoples:
rich food, aged wine,
rich food full of marrow, aged wine well strained.|Preserve all peoples and luxurious repeated food/wine terms.
25:7|On this mountain he will swallow up\nthe covering spread over all peoples,\nthe veil laid over all nations.|Keep swallow verb linking covering with death.

25:8|He will swallow up death forever.
The Lord **GOD** will wipe tears from every face
and remove his people’s disgrace from all the earth,
for the **LORD** has spoken.|Retain death, all faces, and full divine designations.

25:9|On that day people will say,
“Look, this is our God! We waited for him, and he saved us.
This is the **LORD**; we waited for him.
Let us rejoice and be glad in his salvation!”|Repeat waiting and divine identification.

25:10|The **LORD**’s hand will rest on this mountain,\nbut Moab will be trampled where it stands,\nas straw is trampled in a dung pit.|Follow read-form in rather than written water-of; preserve degrading image.

25:11|Moab will spread its hands in it
as a swimmer spreads his hands to swim.
But he will bring down Moab’s pride,
despite the skill of its hands.|Keep swimmer image and uncertain skill expression.
25:12|Your high, fortified walls\nhe has brought down, laid low,\nstruck to the ground, to the dust.|Preserve direct-address shift and cumulative abasement.
26:1|On that day this song will be sung in Judah:\n“We have a strong city!\nHe makes salvation its walls and rampart.|Keep salvation as defenses rather than add named builder.
26:2|Open the gates,\nso a righteous nation may enter,\na nation that keeps faith.|Preserve gate invitation and communal faithfulness.
26:3|You keep in peace—peace—\nthe mind that rests on you,\nbecause it trusts in you.|Make doubled shalom audible without adding perfection.
26:4|Trust in the **LORD** forever,\nfor **YAH**, the **LORD**, is an everlasting rock.|Retain short and full names plus enduring rock.
26:5|He has brought down those who live on high;\nthe lofty city he lays low,\nlays it low to the ground, brings it to the dust.|Repeat lowering of high city.
26:6|Feet trample it—\nthe feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor.”|Preserve formerly weak people as tramplers.
26:7|The path of the righteous is level.\nUpright One, you make the righteous person’s road smooth.|Keep upright address interpretation and road image.
26:8|Along the path of your judgments, **LORD**, we wait for you.\nYour name, your remembrance, is our deepest desire.|Keep judgments as path and name/remembrance pair.

26:9|With my whole being I desire you at night;
with the spirit within me I seek you.
When your judgments are on the earth,
the world’s inhabitants learn righteousness.|Retain night seeking and judgment as instruction.

26:10|Show favor to the wicked, and they still do not learn righteousness.\nIn a land of uprightness they do wrong\nand fail to see the **LORD**’s majesty.|Keep failure despite favor without softening wickedness.
26:11|**LORD**, your hand is raised, but they do not see.\nLet them see your zeal for your people and be ashamed;\nlet the fire for your enemies consume them.|Retain seeing repetition and fiery wish.
26:12|**LORD**, you establish peace for us;\neverything we have accomplished, you have done for us.|Preserve divine agency over our works.
26:13|**LORD** our God, other lords have ruled us;\nbut through you alone we proclaim your name.|Keep contrast of other lords and divine name.

26:14|They are dead; they will not live.
They are shades; they will not rise.
You visited them and destroyed them,
wiping away every memory of them.|Retain dead/shades parallel and finality before verse19 reversal.
26:15|You have enlarged the nation, **LORD**,\nyou have enlarged the nation; you are glorified.\nYou have extended all the land’s boundaries.|Repeat enlargement and preserve land boundaries.
26:16|**LORD**, in distress they sought you;\nthey poured out a whispered prayer\nwhen your discipline was upon them.|Render compressed whisper prayer with uncertainty noted.
26:17|As a pregnant woman near delivery\nwrithes and cries in labor,\nso we were before you, **LORD**.|Preserve labor simile and direct address.

26:18|We conceived, we writhed,
but gave birth only to wind.
We brought no salvation to the earth;
no inhabitants of the world were born.|Retain failed birth and consequential fall/be-born ambiguity.

26:19|Your dead will live; my dead body will rise.
Wake and sing, you who dwell in dust!
Your dew is a dew of light,
and the earth will bring forth the shades.|Preserve unusual my-corpse wording and birth reversal with note.

26:20|Go, my people, enter your rooms
and shut your door behind you.
Hide for a little while,
until the wrath passes.|Follow singular door read-form and temporary shelter.

26:21|Look! The **LORD** comes out from his place
to call earth’s inhabitants to account for their guilt.
The earth will uncover its bloodshed
and no longer conceal its slain.|Keep exposed evidence of violence.

27:1|On that day the **LORD**, with his hard, great, strong sword,
will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent,
Leviathan the twisting serpent,
and kill the monster in the sea.|Retain named monster and three sword descriptions.
27:2|On that day,\n“A delightful vineyard—sing of it!|Follow pinned delightful reading rather than wine-vineyard.

27:3|I, the **LORD**, guard it.
I water it moment by moment;
night and day I guard it
so no one harms it.|Repeat guarding and retain continual watering.

27:4|I have no wrath.
If only briers and thorns confronted me in battle!
I would march against them
and burn them all together.|Preserve wrath denial and hypothetical battle.
27:5|Or let them take hold of my refuge,\nlet them make peace with me—\nmake peace with me.”|Retain alternative refuge and repeated peace.
27:6|In days to come Jacob will take root;\nIsrael will bud and blossom\nand fill the world with fruit.|Keep parallel names and expanding growth.
27:7|Has he struck Jacob as he struck those who struck him?\nHas Jacob been killed as his killers were killed?|Clarify Jacob referent while retaining complex reciprocal question.
27:8|By measured expulsion you contend with her;\nhe drove her away with his harsh wind\non a day of east wind.|Retain difficult measured phrase and you/he shift.

27:9|By this, then, Jacob’s guilt will be atoned for;
this is the full fruit of removing his sin:
when he makes every altar stone like crushed chalk,
and no Asherah poles or incense altars remain standing.|Keep atonement tied to destruction of cult objects.

27:10|The fortified city stands alone,
a settlement deserted and abandoned like the wilderness.
There a calf grazes and lies down,
consuming its branches.|Retain city’s returning animals and stripped growth.
27:12|On that day the **LORD** will thresh\nfrom the River’s flowing waters to the Wadi of Egypt;\nand you, Israelites, will be gathered one by one.|Keep geographical span and individual gathering.

27:13|On that day a great ram’s horn will sound.
Those lost in Assyria and those driven away to Egypt
will come and worship the **LORD**
on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.|Retain two diaspora locations and return to worship.

28:1|Woe to the proud crown of Ephraim’s drunkards,
the fading flower of its glorious beauty,
set above a fertile valley—
to those struck down by wine!|Keep crown/city metaphor and intoxicated people.

28:2|Look! The Lord has someone strong and mighty.
Like a hailstorm, a destructive tempest,
like a torrent of mighty, flooding waters,
he will hurl it to the ground with his hand.|Preserve unnamed agent and storm comparisons.
28:3|The proud crown of Ephraim’s drunkards\nwill be trampled underfoot.|Repeat crown phrase from verse1.

28:4|That fading flower of glorious beauty,
set above a fertile valley,
will be like an early fig before summer:
whoever sees it swallows it
as soon as it reaches the hand.|Keep effortless consumption of first fig.
28:5|On that day the **LORD** of hosts\nwill be a beautiful crown, a glorious wreath,\nfor the remnant of his people,|Preserve reversal from drunkards’ crown to divine crown.
28:6|a spirit of justice for the one who sits in judgment,\nand strength for those who turn battle back at the gate.|Keep judicial and military roles distinct.

28:7|These too reel from wine and stagger from strong drink:
priest and prophet reel from strong drink,
swallowed by wine, staggering from strong drink.
They reel in their visions and stumble in judgment.|Retain accumulated drunkenness and failed guidance.
28:8|Every table is covered with vomit and filth;\nno spot is clean.|Keep disgust without euphemism.

28:9|“Whom is he teaching knowledge?
To whom is he explaining the message?
Children just weaned from milk,
just taken from the breast?|Render mocking questions without invented speaker identity.
28:10|For it is rule upon rule, rule upon rule,\nline upon line, line upon line,\na little here, a little there!”|Preserve repeated syllabic rhythm and note wordplay uncertainty.
28:11|Indeed, with stammering lips and another tongue\nhe will speak to this people,|Keep foreign speech response to mockery.
28:12|to whom he said, “This is rest; let the weary rest.\nThis is refreshment.”\nBut they refused to listen.|Retain rest repetition and refusal.

28:13|So the **LORD**’s word will become for them
rule upon rule, rule upon rule,
line upon line, line upon line,
a little here, a little there—
so they go and stumble backward,
are broken, snared, and captured.|Repeat exact refrain and purposive consequence.
28:14|Therefore hear the **LORD**’s word, you mockers\nwho rule this people in Jerusalem.|Make ruling audience explicit.

28:15|You say, “We have made a covenant with death,
an agreement with Sheol.
When the sweeping scourge passes through, it will not reach us,
for we have made lies our shelter
and hidden ourselves in falsehood.”|Retain rulers’ shocking self-description and mixed flood/scourge image.

28:16|So the Lord **GOD** says:
“Look, I am laying a stone in Zion,
a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a firm foundation.
Whoever trusts will not rush in panic.|Retain tested foundation and haste verb rather than shame.

28:17|I will make justice the measuring line
and righteousness the plumb line.
Hail will sweep away the shelter of lies;
water will flood the hiding place.|Keep building measurements and destroyed false refuge.

28:18|Your covenant with death will be annulled;
your agreement with Sheol will not stand.
When the sweeping scourge passes through,
you will be trampled beneath it.|Repeat covenant language and violent undoing.

28:19|Every time it passes through, it will take you.\nMorning after morning it will pass through, by day and by night.\nUnderstanding the message will bring sheer terror.”|Retain recurrence and message-understanding reversal.
28:20|The bed is too short to stretch out on;\nthe blanket too narrow to wrap yourself in.|Keep concrete inadequate shelter proverb.

28:21|The **LORD** will rise as at Mount Perazim,
will rage as in Gibeon’s valley,
to do his deed—his strange deed,
to perform his work—his foreign work.|Preserve unusual divine work and named battle echoes.
28:22|Now stop mocking, lest your bonds grow tighter.\nFor I have heard from the Lord **GOD** of hosts\nof destruction decreed against all the earth.|Retain authorized warning and scope.
28:23|Listen closely to my voice;\npay attention and hear what I say.|Keep paired appeals before farming instruction.
28:24|Does a plowman plow all day to sow,\ncontinually opening and harrowing his soil?|Retain rhetorical limit on preparatory labor.
28:25|Once he has leveled its surface, does he not scatter black cumin,\nsow cumin, plant wheat in rows,\nbarley in its place, and spelt along the edge?|Preserve five crops and differentiated sowing.
28:26|His God instructs him in the right way\nand teaches him.|Keep agricultural skill as divine teaching.

28:27|Black cumin is not threshed with a threshing sledge,
nor is a cartwheel rolled over cumin.
Black cumin is beaten with a stick,
and cumin with a rod.|Retain different tools and repeated spice names.

28:28|Grain for bread is crushed,
but one does not thresh it forever.
He drives his cartwheel and horses over it
without grinding it to pieces.|Retain difficult crushing distinction with note.
28:29|This too comes from the **LORD** of hosts,\nwonderful in counsel, great in resourcefulness.|Connect skill and wise counsel without sermon.
29:1|Woe, Ariel, Ariel, city where David camped!\nAdd year to year; let the festivals come around.|Keep repeated symbolic name and liturgical cycle.
29:2|I will press Ariel hard;\nthere will be mourning and moaning.\nShe will become like an altar hearth to me.|Expose Ariel wordplay while noting uncertain sense.
29:3|I will encamp all around you,\nlay siege to you with posts,\nand raise siegeworks against you.|Keep first-person divine siege and equipment.

29:4|Brought low, you will speak from the ground;
your words will sink into the dust.
Your voice will come from the ground like a ghost’s,
your speech will chirp from the dust.|Preserve ghostlike reduced voice and dust repetition.
29:5|Yet the throng of your foreigners will become fine dust,\nthe throng of the ruthless like drifting chaff.\nSuddenly, in an instant,|Retain abrupt reversal and unnamed foreigners.
29:6|the **LORD** of hosts will visit you\nwith thunder, earthquake, and great noise,\nwhirlwind, tempest, and devouring flame.|Preserve visitation rather than specify rescue within verb.

29:7|The throng of all nations fighting Ariel,
all who wage war against her and her stronghold,
all who press her hard,
will be like a dream, a vision at night.|Keep siege forces becoming insubstantial.

29:8|As a hungry person dreams of eating
and wakes with an empty stomach,
as a thirsty person dreams of drinking
and wakes faint and still thirsty,
so will be the throng of all nations
fighting Mount Zion.|Retain both unsatisfied appetite dreams.

29:9|Stupefy yourselves and be stupefied!
Blind yourselves and be blind!
They are drunk, but not from wine;
they stagger, but not from strong drink.|Keep commands then third-person observation.
29:10|For the **LORD** has poured over you a spirit of deep sleep.\nHe has closed your eyes—the prophets—\nand covered your heads—the seers.|Preserve eyes/heads identified with prophetic figures.

29:11|For you the whole vision has become like the words of a sealed scroll. Give it to someone who can read and say, “Please read this,” and the answer is, “I cannot; it is sealed.”|Make literacy scene intelligible without removing sealed-scroll metaphor.
29:12|Give the scroll to someone who cannot read and say, “Please read this,” and the answer is, “I cannot read.”|Keep second distinct inability and repeated request.

29:13|The Lord said:
“This people approaches me with its mouth
and honors me with its lips,
but its heart is far from me.
Its fear of me is a human command learned by rote.|Retain mouth/lips/heart contrast and taught reverence.

29:14|So I will again astound this people,
with wonder upon wonder.
The wisdom of its wise will perish,
and the discernment of its discerning will disappear.”|Keep repeated wonders and failed wisdom.
29:15|Woe to those who bury their plans deep from the **LORD**,\nwhose deeds are done in darkness,\nwho say, “Who sees us? Who knows us?”|Retain concealment depth and paired questions.

29:16|You turn things upside down!
Should the potter be regarded as clay?
Should a thing made say of its maker, “He did not make me,”
or a formed thing say of its former, “He has no understanding”?|Keep creator/creation reversal and two denials.
29:17|In just a little while,\nwill not Lebanon become fruitful land,\nand fruitful land be regarded as forest?|Preserve landscape reversal without imposed allegory.
29:18|On that day the deaf will hear a scroll’s words,\nand out of gloom and darkness\nthe eyes of the blind will see.|Link inaccessible scroll to restored hearing.
29:19|The lowly will find fresh joy in the **LORD**;\nthe poorest people will rejoice in Israel’s Holy One.|Retain social lowliness and Holy One designation.
29:20|For the ruthless will be gone, the mocker finished,\nand all who watch for a chance to do evil will be cut off—|Keep three groups and watchfulness for wrong.

29:21|those who make a person guilty by a word,\nset a trap for the one who argues a case at the gate,\nand with empty claims deny justice to the righteous.|Preserve corrupt judicial setting and word ambiguity.

29:22|Therefore the **LORD**, who redeemed Abraham, says to Jacob’s house:\n“Jacob will no longer be ashamed;\nhis face will no longer grow pale.|Keep Abraham redemption statement and collective Jacob.

29:23|When he sees his children, the work of my hands, in his midst,
they will honor my name as holy;
they will honor Jacob’s Holy One as holy
and stand in awe of Israel’s God.|Preserve shifts between Jacob and children and holiness repetition.
29:24|Those whose spirits wander will gain understanding;\nthose who grumble will learn instruction.”|Retain two restored responses.

30:1|“Woe to rebellious children,” declares the **LORD**,
“who carry out plans that are not mine,
who make an alliance without my Spirit,
adding sin to sin.|Choose alliance sense for pouring/covering phrase and note ambiguity.
30:2|They go down to Egypt without asking my counsel,\nseeking refuge in Pharaoh’s protection,\nshelter in Egypt’s shade.|Keep unauthorized journey and paired protection images.
30:3|But Pharaoh’s protection will bring you shame,\nand shelter in Egypt’s shade, humiliation.|Repeat protection terms with reversal.
30:4|Though his officials are in Zoan\nand his messengers reach Hanes,|Keep his uncertain referent and two Egyptian places.
30:5|all are put to shame by a people who cannot benefit them,\nwho offer neither help nor advantage,\nonly shame and disgrace.”|Follow shame read-form and repeated failed benefit.

30:6|An oracle concerning the beasts of the Negeb:
Through a land of distress and hardship,
of lioness and lion, viper and flying fiery serpent,
they carry wealth on donkeys’ shoulders,
treasures on camels’ humps,
to a people who cannot benefit them.|Keep burden/oracle heading, all animals, and costly embassy.
30:7|Egypt’s help is breath and emptiness;\nso I call her “Rahab, sitting still.”|Retain breath, symbolic Rahab, and inactive boast.

30:8|Now go, write it on a tablet before them,
inscribe it on a scroll,
so it may remain for a coming day,
forever and ever.|Retain dual writing media and future testimony without emendation.
30:9|For they are a rebellious people, lying children,\nchildren unwilling to hear the **LORD**’s instruction.|Keep children repetition and refusal to hear.

30:10|They say to those who see, “Do not see!”
and to the seers, “Do not see straight for us!
Tell us smooth things;
see illusions.|Retain ironic commands addressed to seers.
30:11|Leave the way! Turn aside from the path!\nGet Israel’s Holy One out of our sight!”|Keep path pair and shocking dismissal.

30:12|So Israel’s Holy One says:
“Because you reject this word
and trust in oppression and crookedness,
leaning on them,|Preserve rejected word and chosen dependencies.
30:13|this guilt will be like a widening breach\nbulging in a high wall,\nwhose collapse comes suddenly, in an instant.|Keep visible structural failure image.

30:14|It will shatter like a potter’s jar,
crushed without mercy,
not a shard among its fragments large enough
to scoop fire from a hearth
or dip water from a cistern.”|Preserve two mundane uses lost in total destruction.

30:15|For the Lord **GOD**, Israel’s Holy One, says:
“In returning and rest you will be saved;
in quietness and trust will be your strength.”
But you were unwilling.|Retain returning rather than silently specify conversion.

30:16|You said, “No! We will flee on horses!”
Therefore you will flee.
“We will ride swift mounts!”
Therefore your pursuers will be swift.|Keep matching boast and consequence verbs.

30:17|A thousand will flee at one person’s threat;
at the threat of five you will flee,
until what remains of you is like a mast on a mountaintop,
like a signal on a hill.|Preserve thousand/one/five and isolated mast.

30:18|Yet the **LORD** waits to show you favor;
he rises to have compassion on you.
For the **LORD** is a God of justice.
Happy are all who wait for him!|Keep reciprocal waiting and second divine name.

30:19|People in Zion, dwelling in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely show you favor at the sound of your cry; as soon as he hears, he will answer.|Make collective address readable; preserve immediate answer.

30:20|Though the Lord gives you bread of distress and water of oppression, your Teacher will no longer hide; your eyes will see your Teacher.|Choose singular teacher from contextual verb and note plural possibility.
30:21|Your ears will hear a word behind you: “This is the way; walk in it,” whenever you turn right or left.|Keep guidance from behind and both directions.

30:22|You will defile the silver plating of your carved idols and the gold covering of your cast images. You will scatter them like a menstrual cloth and say, “Away with you!”|Retain menstrual comparison rather than generic unclean thing.

30:23|He will give rain for the seed you sow in the soil, and the soil’s grain will be rich and plentiful. On that day your livestock will graze in spacious pasture.|Preserve soil repetition and abundant food for people/animals.
30:24|The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat seasoned fodder, winnowed with shovel and fork.|Retain quality fodder and both implements.
30:25|On every high mountain and lofty hill there will be streams of running water, on the day of great slaughter when the towers fall.|Keep slaughter alongside restored water.

30:26|The moon’s light will be like the sun’s, and the sun’s light seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, when the **LORD** binds his people’s fracture and heals the wound from his blow.|Preserve sevenfold light and injury attributed to divine blow.

30:27|Look! The name of the **LORD** comes from afar,
his anger burning, his burden heavy.
His lips are full of indignation,
his tongue like devouring fire.|Retain coming name and difficult burden expression.

30:28|His breath is like a flooding stream rising to the neck,\nsifting nations in a sieve of destruction;\na bridle that leads astray is on the peoples’ jaws.|Keep three judgment images and misleading bridle.

30:29|You will have a song as on a night when a festival is consecrated,\nand gladness of heart like those who go with a flute\nto the **LORD**’s mountain, to Israel’s Rock.|Preserve festival-night setting and divine Rock.

30:30|The **LORD** will make his majestic voice heard
and show his arm descending,
with furious anger and devouring flame,
cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.|Keep arm action and weather catalogue.
30:31|At the **LORD**’s voice Assyria will be shattered;\nhe will strike with the rod.|Keep divine strike and named target.

30:32|Every stroke of the appointed staff
that the **LORD** brings down upon him
will be accompanied by tambourines and lyres;
with swinging blows he will battle them.|Preserve him/them shift following read-form plural.

30:33|Topheth has long been prepared;
it is made ready even for the king.
Its fire pit is deep and wide,
with fire and wood in abundance.
The **LORD**’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, sets it ablaze.|Retain prepared burning place and sulfur breath.

31:1|Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help,
leaning on horses,
trusting chariots because they are many
and horsemen because they are very strong,
but not looking to Israel’s Holy One
or seeking the **LORD**!|Keep military abundance contrasted with unasked divine help.

31:2|Yet he too is wise; he brings disaster
and does not take back his words.
He will rise against the house of evildoers
and against the helpers of those who do wrong.|Preserve ironic wisdom and culpable helpers.

31:4|For the **LORD** said this to me:
“As a lion, a young lion, growls over its prey,
though a whole band of shepherds is called against it,
not frightened by their voices
nor subdued by their uproar,
so the **LORD** of hosts will descend
to fight on Mount Zion and its hill.|Retain lion resolve and open force of on/for/against Zion.
31:6|Return to the one against whom you Israelites have rebelled so deeply.|Make addressed people explicit within return appeal.
31:7|On that day each of you will reject the silver idols and gold idols your own hands made for you as a sin.|Keep human manufacture and paired metals.

31:8|“Assyria will fall by a sword not of man;
a sword not of humanity will devour him.
He will flee before the sword,
and his young men will become forced laborers.|Preserve nonhuman sword and enslavement aftermath.

31:9|His rock will pass away in terror;
his officials will panic at the signal,”
declares the **LORD**, whose fire is in Zion,
whose furnace is in Jerusalem.|Keep uncertain rock metaphor and divine furnace.
32:1|Look! A king will reign in righteousness,\nand officials will govern with justice.|Keep righteous rule and distinct governing roles.

32:2|Each will be like a shelter from wind,
a refuge from a storm,
like streams in a dry place,
